Answer: **Economics**. In the Economics discipline the majority of authors are male in both original and replication studies more consistently than in any other discipline: 77.8% (14/18) of original studies and 72.2% (13/18) of replications have a majority of male authors (authors_male.o > 0.5 and authors_male.r > 0.5), with the highest mean male-author ratios of all disciplines (mean authors_male.o = 0.87, mean authors_male.r = 0.84). If ties (ratio = 0.5) count as majority-male, Economics reaches 100% of originals and 83.3% of replications.

Full per-discipline table (strict >0.5 | ≥0.5):
- Economics (n=18): majority-male 77.8% | 100% of originals; 72.2% | 83.3% of replications; mean ratio 0.87 | 0.84
- Cognitive (n=241): 75.9% | 88.0% originals; 52.7% | 61.4% replications; mean 0.77 | 0.51
- Social (n=668): 56.6% | 98.4% originals; 53.1% | 60.9% replications; mean 0.73 | 0.51

Hypothesis: In the Economics domain, the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies — Economics has the largest share of studies with a majority of male authors on both sides (authors_male.o and authors_male.r > 0.5) and the highest average male-author ratios, whereas in Cognitive and Social the male majority in replications is only marginal (just above 50%).
